title: He Took 60 Wickets and Won J&K Their First Ranji Trophy. Now He's on the India A Plane to Sri Lanka.
excerpt: Auqib Nabi's selection for the multi-day tour of Sri Lanka caps an unprecedented rise from Jammu & Kashmir's domestic cricket to the national pipeline.
body:
Auqib Nabi took 60 wickets in a single Ranji Trophy season. He led Jammu & Kashmir to their first-ever title. On Saturday, the BCCI named him in the India A squad for the upcoming tour of Sri Lanka.

The announcement came alongside the naming of wicketkeeper-batter Dhruv Jurel as India A captain for two four-day matches against Sri Lanka A in Galle, starting June 25. Devdutt Padikkal will serve as vice-captain. But the most significant selection in the 14-man squad is Nabi's — a fast-bowling all-rounder from a region that until this year had never won a major domestic title.

## From Net Bowler to Squad Member in a Week

Just days ago, Nabi was bowling in the nets to India's Test squad at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur, helping the senior team prepare for the one-off Test against Afghanistan. Alongside left-arm spinner Zeeshan Ansari, he served as a net bowler — the lowest rung on Indian cricket's professional ladder, where you bowl at the best in the world and then sit in the stands to watch them bat.

Now both Nabi and Ansari have been selected for India A. The net bowler has become a squad member.

## J&K's Unprecedented Ranji Season

The backdrop to Nabi's selection is Jammu & Kashmir's extraordinary 2025-26 Ranji Trophy campaign. For decades, J&K cricket existed on the margins of Indian domestic cricket — a team known more for its logistical challenges than its results. Matches were frequently shifted out of the state for security reasons. Infrastructure was minimal. The path from Srinagar to the Indian team felt impossibly long.

This season, everything changed. Nabi, a right-arm medium-fast bowler with genuine swing and seam movement, took 60 wickets at an average that made national selectors take notice. His figures were not just the best in the tournament — they were the best by a J&K bowler in any Ranji Trophy season in the state's history.

The team rallied around his performances. They beat established sides — teams with IPL contracts and international experience — on their way to the final. And then they won it. The celebrations in Srinagar were scenes that Indian cricket rarely produces: an entire region's worth of joy compressed into a single trophy lift.

## The India A Squad

The full squad reads like a showcase of India's next Test generation:

**Dhruv Jurel (captain)**, Sai Sudharsan, Ayush Badoni, **Devdutt Padikkal (vice-captain)**, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Saransh Jain, Gurnoor Brar, **Auqib Nabi**, Yash Thakur, Anshul Kamboj, N Jagadeesan, Aman Mokhade, Shaik Rasheed, and Zeeshan Ansari.

Several of these players — Gaikwad, Badoni, Thakur, and Kamboj — are already in Sri Lanka for the 50-over tri-series beginning June 9 in Dambulla. The multi-day matches will follow from June 25 in Galle, ahead of India's senior two-Test WTC series against Sri Lanka in August.

## Why It Matters for the Diaspora

For the Kashmiri diaspora — spread across the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf — Nabi's selection carries a weight that transcends cricket. Kashmir's relationship with India has been defined by conflict, Article 370's abrogation, and political tension. A J&K cricketer earning national recognition through sheer domestic dominance offers a narrative that cuts through the usual discourse.

Cricket has always been Kashmir's escape valve. The Dal Lake pickup games, the street cricket in Lal Chowk, the boys who bowl fast on pitches that barely deserve the name — Nabi comes from that tradition. His India A cap says something that politics alone cannot: that the system, at its best, rewards performance regardless of geography.

## What's Next

The Galle pitches will test Nabi in conditions vastly different from the green tops of domestic Indian cricket. Sri Lanka's spin-friendly surfaces and the Kookaburra ball will demand adaptation. But Nabi's selection is not about what happens in Galle alone. It is about what it means that he is on the plane at all.

Sixty wickets. One title. One call-up. The boy from J&K is on his way.

*Sources: BCCI Squad Announcement, IANS, CricketAddictor, The Daily Jagran, SportsTak*
